chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Haysam al-Ajali (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qattan said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Hussein ibn Mus'ab, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Blowing is detestable at three things: at talismans (ruqas), at food, and at the place of prostration.
ai.seo_question: What are the three things upon which blowing is considered detestable in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies three specific locations where blowing is considered detestable (makruh): on ruqas (amulets), food, and the place of prostration (sujood). This ruling distinguishes between the general etiquette of blowing for healing or blessing and the specific act of blowing on these items, which may imply a subtle form of superstition or distraction from divine reliance. The prohibition on blowing on the place of sujood underscores the sanctity of the prayer posture, ensuring that the physical act does not detract from the spiritual focus of the worshipper.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-203 Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qat’tan quoted Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qat’tan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Mus’ab that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
Blowing at three things is detestable: blowing at a talisman, blowing at food, and blowing at the place of prostration.”
